title: "Impact of a TB epidemic on worker and firm productivity: the regional perspective from Ukraine"

Tuberculosis remains a significant regional health burden in Ukraine, with
prevalence varying sharply across oblasts. We link regional TB incidence
to worker- and firm-level productivity outcomes using administrative
records from 2003–2009, finding that higher disease prevalence reduced
both worker wages and firm total factor productivity, with substantial
spillover effects across neighbouring regions. A 10% reduction in
prevalence is estimated to raise GDP by roughly 1.05% — far exceeding the
0.04% of GDP spent on TB control that year, evidence with direct relevance
to postwar health and labour policy.

**Published in:** *Journal of Population Economics*, 39, article 63 (2026)
